source.title: A circuit mechanism for differentiating positive and negative associations

confidence_rationale: This is a direct measurement of the ARC-121 crux from the opposing (dissociable-systems) side. Rather than showing that harm and reward evaluation share a common representation, Namburi et al. demonstrate that within a single anatomical structure (basolateral amygdala) positive (reward) and negative (fear) associations are computed by ANATOMICALLY and SYNAPTICALLY dissociable, opposing projection-defined circuits: neurons projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc) undergo plasticity supporting positive reinforcement, while a distinct population projecting to centromedial amygdala (CeM) undergoes opposing plasticity supporting negative (fear) reinforcement, and these are CAUSALLY separable -- photostimulating one drives reward-like behavior, photostimulating the other drives fear-like behavior, and inhibiting the fear-coding population both impairs fear conditioning AND enhances reward conditioning (a genuine double dissociation with a competitive interaction, not mere independence). This directly weakens a strong reading of ARC-121: harm/threat evaluation and reward valuation, even when co-located in the same gross anatomical region, are implemented by structurally distinct, competing circuits rather than reading a single shared state.
failure_signatures: The dissociation shown is WITHIN the amygdala's input stage (BLA projection populations), which is upstream of the vmPFC/ventral-striatum 'common currency' hub that the supporting entries in this directory (Bartra 2013, Shenhav 2010, Koenigs 2007) implicate -- it is possible both readings are simultaneously true at different stages of processing: dissociable circuits COMPUTE positive vs. negative associations at the amygdala input stage, but a shared representation is then FORMED downstream at vmPFC/ventral striatum for integration into decisions (including moral ones). This entry does not resolve that staged-architecture possibility, and a future pull specifically on amygdala-to-vmPFC convergence would be needed to adjudicate it.

This study is rodent Pavlovian fear/reward conditioning, not human harm/ethics moral judgment -- the transfer from 'BLA circuit-level dissociation between simple fear and reward conditioning' to REE's E3/harm-goal-error and moral-evaluation construct is substantial and should not be over-read as a direct refutation of ARC-121's specific claim.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Within the basolateral amygdala, two projection-defined neuronal populations -- those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc) and those projecting to centromedial amygdala (CeM) -- undergo opposing synaptic plasticity following fear versus reward conditioning, and are causally and competitively dissociable: activating NAc-projectors supports positive reinforcement, activating CeM-projectors supports negative reinforcement, and inhibiting CeM-projectors both impairs fear learning and enhances reward learning.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-121 claims harm/ethics evaluation converges on the SAME shared epistemic-state object that prediction, replay, planning and learning consume, rather than maintaining its own private, mechanism-specific stream. Namburi et al. supply a genuine counterweight: at least at the amygdala's input stage, positive (reward-adjacent) and negative (harm/threat-adjacent) evaluation are computed by anatomically and synaptically SEPARATE, mutually competitive circuits -- exactly the 'dissociable systems' alternative the chip's brief explicitly asked to be searched for, not merely a shared-state readout gated differently downstream.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is upstream, subcortical, rodent Pavlovian circuitry (BLA input-stage dissociation between simple fear and reward conditioning), not human moral/ethics judgment and not necessarily the same processing stage as the vmPFC/ventral-striatum hub the supporting entries in this directory implicate. A staged-architecture reconciliation (dissociable at BLA input, convergent at vmPFC integration) is plausible but untested by this paper alone -- treat this as a genuine complication for ARC-121's strong reading, not a refutation of the whole claim.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; optogenetic circuit-specific manipulation combined with ex vivo electrophysiology and Pavlovian fear/reward conditioning; projection-defined BLA neuron populations (NAc-projecting vs. CeM-projecting).

confidence_components.notes: High source quality: landmark Nature paper with strong causal (optogenetic) circuit dissection, widely cited as foundational for valence-specific amygdala circuitry. Mapping fidelity moderate: it directly measures dissociable positive/negative circuits at the amygdala input stage, which is the right kind of measurement for the ARC-121 crux question, but the anatomical level (BLA input, rodent, simple conditioning) is one stage removed from the vmPFC/ventral-striatum integration hub and from human moral judgment specifically.
